verdict.rationale: Asaas documents the building blocks of a self-serve payment integration: simple API-key auth, an API reference whose try-it requests run in Sandbox, and a Sandbox walkthrough for creating charges, simulating payment and receiving the Webhook. The evidence never shows copy-paste code samples in multiple languages, official SDKs, or any proof of time-to-first-payment. missing for 10: copy-paste code examples in multiple programming languages, SDKs or quickstart snippets, independent or hands-on evidence of integrating in under a day.

support.subject: As a developer, I can integrate a working payment flow from the docs alone in under a day, with copy-paste examples in my language

citations.quote: The Asaas API uses an API key to identify the account responsible for the request. Send the key in the access_token header.
Tests run directly from the API reference use the Sandbox environment.
You can test flows such as creating customers, charges, payments, transfers, and Webhooks before using Production credentials.
Simulate the payment in the Sandbox. Receive the corresponding Webhook event.
create payments, process card payments at creation time or later, and capture payments with pre-authorization.
